decisions.executionNote: Begin elbow-up approach to leftmost toy car; assign cars to white, watches to blue, pens to red. Grasp geometry will be refined from wrist view.
Lower and tilt left gripper toward cyan car, keeping fingers open and approach in left workspace.
Fine approach and close on cyan car. Wrist view suggests small leftward and forward correction before grasp.
Hold closed, lift cyan car clear, then carry toward white basket; check visual retention.
Cyan car visibly retained. Move above white basket interior, lower slightly and open, then begin clearance lift.
Cyan car settled in white basket. Lift free and approach yellow toy car from above, left arm staying on its side.
Align left fingers across yellow car's narrower width and descend gradually; keep clearance from adjacent red car and watch.
Correct yellow car centering from wrist image, lower to body height and close. A short lift will test retention visually.
Lift yellow car with closed fingers and transport above white basket, gradually realigning the wrist. Verify retention from RGB.
Yellow car visibly retained. Replan slower translation and yaw after continuity guard, carrying it over white basket.
Release yellow car inside white basket and lift clear; start approaching remaining red car with left arm.
Approach red car from the left side of center with open fingers. Yellow and cyan cars are visible inside white basket.
Descend and close across red car body while keeping left EE just left of center. Lift slightly to check grasp.
Red car was not securely between fingers. Reopen, advance slightly and lower to body level, then reclose and test a small lift.
Red car now appears between fingers. Maintain closure, lift clear and carry leftward toward white basket with continuous elbow-up posture.
Red car slipped/remained on table. Reapproach with a more vertical, length-aligned grasp to pinch its narrower sides, staying left of center.
Visual servo red car toward the finger midline and descend with fingers open; use wrist view to establish actual grasp depth.
Red car is centered between open fingers. Lower a little, close on its sides, then lift vertically to verify retention before transfer.
Red car visibly pinched and lifted. Carry slowly toward white basket without changing wrist orientation; keep gripper closed.
Move retained red car fully over white basket interior, accounting for its hanging rear end. Keep closed until safely inside rim.
Guard interrupted near basket; red car appears to have slipped toward the rim. Back away with smaller increments and relax wrist tilt to regain configuration margin, then reassess.
Red car is outside white basket on its side. Reorient for a narrow-side regrasp in front of the basket, keeping left arm elbow-up.
Refine red car alignment from wrist view and lower slowly to grasp its exposed side, avoiding the basket rim.
Move fingers away from basket rim and center across the overturned red car, then close gently and test lift.
Tracking indicates rim interference. Lift open fingers clear before shifting rearward to center on red car; do not force the obstructed descent.
Red car is now centered with rim clearance. Descend onto its exposed sides, close fully, and make a small test lift.
Correct slight lateral misalignment and deepen grasp on overturned red car. Reopen before adjustment, then close and lift vertically.
Test retention by lifting vertically well above rim, then begin a slow leftward transfer with fingers fully closed.
Car remained on table. Reopen and approach lower at a corrected center; previous closures appear too high to capture the body.
Advance along approach direction to grasp lower on the red car sides rather than above the chassis; close and test lift.
Car sides appear securely between fingers. Lift vertically to clear the basket rim before any substantial transfer.
Red car retained through lift. Carry it above the white basket center at rim-clearing height, keeping the same grasp orientation.
Red car is above white basket interior. Release without further forward motion, then retreat in small increments after the continuity guard.
All three cars are inside white basket. Approach green watch with left arm and begin elbow-up preparation of right arm for pens.
Lower left fingers toward green watch. Use right arm for the other watch in its own workspace; approach both with open grippers.
Center both watch bands between the fingers, lower slightly, close fully and perform small test lifts; retention still needs visual confirmation.
Lift both watches with closed fingers and begin slow inward transport. Keep arms separated and verify each watch moves with its gripper.
Both watches remain in the grips. Move green watch over the left half of blue basket while silver watch approaches from the right, preserving arm separation.
Release green watch into blue basket, then withdraw left arm. Bring retained silver watch over the right half of blue without crossing arms.
Release silver watch into blue and retreat right. Reorient left gripper to approach the left white pen; it will need a center staging transfer for right-side sorting.
Replan with smaller rotations after guard. Lower left toward white pen and align right for the upper white pen; both watches are visibly inside blue.
Fine-align and close left on the first white pen. Continue aligning right fingers across the upper white pen while descending slowly.
Correct left pen's slight lateral miss and grasp lower. Center right gripper on upper white pen, close, then test small lifts for both.
Lift retained left white pen and start rotating for a center staging placement. Reopen right and correct its lateral miss before closing lower on the other white pen.
Left pen stays retained; rotate and move toward a center staging spot without crossing. Right grasp appears too high: reopen, descend further and recenter slightly before reclosing.
Stage left white pen near center for right-arm pickup, then lift open. Right fingers are aligned but likely too high; lower another small amount, close and test retention.
Left pen is staged; withdraw left arm clear of center. Right closure still misses the pen vertically, so descend with open fingers along its approach, close at table level and test lift.
Lift right white pen clear to verify grasp, then carry toward red basket. Return empty left arm toward its origin with continuous elbow-up motion.
Shift retained white pen fully inside red basket boundaries and release. Finish returning the empty left arm to its initial pose.
First white pen is inside red basket. Withdraw right arm and reorient above the black pen, keeping left arm at origin.
Advance the open right gripper along the black pen's length and lower toward it; refine grasp from the wrist view before closing.
Black pen is aligned between the open fingers. Lower to its shaft height, close fully, and test a small lift before transporting.
Fingers may be contacting the table. Lift slowly while maintaining closure to clear interference and visually test whether the black pen is captured.
Black pen is visibly retained. Lift and carry it toward red basket, gradually rotating the wrist to place it without overextending.
Move black pen fully over red basket, rotate its long axis away from the rim, lower slightly and release. One staged white pen remains.
Black and first white pen are in red basket. Lift clear and bring right arm toward the last staged white pen, rotating to align across its shaft.
Align right gripper with the last white pen and descend with fingers open, keeping the right EE on its side of center.
Last white pen is aligned with the finger midline. Descend to shaft height, close fully and test retention with a small vertical lift.
Pen remains on table; closure was above its shaft. Reopen and lower further at the same alignment, then close and lift gently.
Fingers appear obstructed at table level. Lift gradually while maintaining closure to clear contact and test whether the last pen is retained.
Last pen was not lifted. Correct a slight lateral miss and close at an intermediate height above the table, then test a small lift.
Pen appears between finger pads. Lift vertically with closure maintained, then make a small rightward motion to verify retention in RGB.
Last pen stayed on the table. Reopen and approach farther along its shaft, rather than closing near the tip; keep right EE positive.
Correct the pen's lateral offset from the finger midline, close at the current low height, and lift vertically to test capture.
The pen is not retained. Switch to a more vertical grasp to reduce fingertip/table interference, opening first and keeping the right arm on its side.
Correct the tilt direction for a near-vertical pinch, targeting the accessible right end of the last white pen with open fingers.
With near-vertical fingers, center over the thicker part near the pen's right end and descend before closing. Right EE remains positive; left stays at origin.
Relieve slight table contact, allow fingers time to close around the centered shaft, then lift vertically with closure maintained.
Previous closure still appears above the shaft. With fingers now almost vertical, descend to a lower pinch height while open, then close and pause before lifting.
Table contact blocked the descent. Lift a few millimeters to clear it and correct the small lateral offset, then close at that height and test a gentle lift.
Wrist view shows the pen left of the closing midline. Correct the lateral direction, reopen before moving, then close on the shaft and test lift.
Center is aligned but the pinch is near the tapered tip. Move open fingers along the pen to a thicker section and slightly lower, then close and test.
Pen shifted slightly to the right in the wrist view. Reopen and correct a few millimeters across the shaft, then close slowly and lift to verify.
No retention after lift. Return to an oblique shaft grasp, compensating wrist position for the fingertip offset and keeping fingers open.
Center the white shaft laterally under the right fingers, descend a small amount and close slowly. Pause before testing retention.
